content: Tincture of iodine typically consists of 10% elemental iodine dissolved in ethanol, although it is also available in concentrations of 2%, 3%, and 7%. It is a critical component of any emergency survival kit, serving dual purposes: disinfecting wounds and sanitizing surface water to make it safe for drinking. In situations where an alcohol-based solution is not suitable, alternatives such as Lugol's iodine (an aqueous solution of iodine in potassium iodide) or povidone-iodine (commonly known as Betadine, a PVP-I solution) can be used. Additionally, iodine can be employed to detect and treat iodine deficiency, a condition that may result in hypothyroidism. It is important to note that iodine is toxic. Children and pregnant women, who are more sensitive to its effects, should avoid its use. The human body requires only trace amounts of iodine for proper metabolic function, which is typically fulfilled by consuming iodized salt. When using iodine to sanitize surface water, the treated water should be left to sit for 30 minutes before consumption to ensure that all viruses and bacteria are effectively killed. If the water temperature is below 20°C (68°F), the sitting time should be extended to several hours to achieve adequate disinfection. For this purpose, 0.1 oz of 2% tincture of iodine is recommended. Alternatively, iodine for water sanitization is also available in tablet or crystal form. These forms of iodine can often be found at health stores or through trip outfitters.
